description:
THE HIGH GROUND HAS MOVED.

We do not wait for orbital commands.

We chart the unmapped frontier at machine speed.
summary: ARES-NAV is a browser-based 3D Mars mission planner set in Gale Crater and Mount Sharp. It combines terrain built from real elevation data with five orbital map layers (optical, topographic, spectral, thermal and radiation) and plans safe walking routes between mission waypoints, avoiding steep slopes and boulder fields. A helmet visor mode shows oxygen, battery and slope readouts in first person, and live NASA data such as solar flares and Curiosity updates is pulled in. During a solar flare, the plan switches to a return route to a shielded lava tube. This matters because safe surface missions depend on understanding terrain, resources and radiation before anyone steps outside, and ARES-NAV makes that planning visual, interactive and available in any browser.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?
ARES-NAV is a browser-based 3D Mars mission planner set in Gale Crater and Mount Sharp. It builds the terrain from real elevation data and adds five orbital map layers: optical, topographic, spectral, thermal and radiation. A slope-aware pathfinding algorithm plans safe walking routes between mission waypoints. A helmet visor mode gives a first-person view with oxygen, battery and slope readouts, and the app pulls in live NASA data such as solar flares and Curiosity updates.

What benefits does it have?
It helps plan safer surface missions. Routes avoid steep slopes and boulder fields, and the plan tracks oxygen, battery and radiation dose. It runs in a browser with nothing to install.

What is the intended impact of the project?
The goal is to make mission planning easier to understand and prepare for. If a solar flare hits, the plan switches to a return route to a shielded lava tube, which has about 60% less radiation dose, so crews can see their options before they head out.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript and Three.js (WebGL), with procedural terrain math (fbm) and Chaikin curve smoothing. A Python script prepared the terrain files. Git and GitHub were used for version control, Netlify for hosting, and Claude and Gemini for AI-assisted development. No special hardware is needed, only a browser with WebGL.

How is your project creative?
Instead of static maps, routes are planned from real elevation data and hazard zones, and the result is interactive in 3D. It also has an animated loading sequence in which a globe slides into place and hands off to the main app.
